variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)

/-- **The widened cover datum** (R2, human decision I-0492): finitely many **arbitrary
affine opens** of the relative curve that **jointly** cover it.

Contrast with `FinCoverData`, which this replaces on the certificate side: there is no `h₀`,
no `h₁`, no `a₀`/`a₁`, no `partition₀`/`partition₁`, no `Sum` index, and above all no typing
of a piece into a pinned chart.  The chart-wise partitions of unity are exactly what upgraded
per-piece swallow-or-miss to a chart statement, and they are gone deliberately; the two-chart
structure the Θ-layer needs is carried separately (see `ChartTyping` below), never by the
certificate clauses.

`Type u`, like `FinCoverData`, so a functor value can quotient it. -/
structure AffCoverData : Type u where
  /-- The number of pieces. -/
  m : ℕ
  /-- The pieces: arbitrary opens of the relative curve, made affine by `isAffineOpen`. -/
  pieces : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens
  /-- Every piece is affine — the only geometric demand the certificate layer makes. -/
  isAffineOpen : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (pieces j)
  /-- The pieces cover the curve JOINTLY.  This replaces the two chart-wise partitions of
  unity, and it is the whole structural content of the widening. -/
  cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤

namespace AffCoverData

variable {C R π} (D : AffCoverData C R)

/-- The gluing index of the widened datum: a bare `Fin`, with no two-sided structure. -/
abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m

/-- **Every point lies in a piece.** Under `FinCoverData` this came from `relCover_sup`
together with the two partitions of unity; here it is exactly the joint covering field —
obligation I-0492 4(ii) discharged in one line rather than silently supplied by the typing. -/
lemma exists_mem_pieces (z : relCurve C R) : ∃ j : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces j := by
  have hz : z ∈ (⨆ j, D.pieces j) := by rw [D.cover]; trivial
  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mp hz

/-- The pieces are affine opens — by fiat now, rather than as basic opens of an affine
chart. -/
lemma isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) :=
  D.isAffineOpen j

/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring.** The widened replacement for
`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/
theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) :=
  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)

/-- Piece overlaps are affine (the relative curve is separated over `Spec R`, being proper),
so the overlap section rings are flat too — the widened
`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf`. -/
theorem flat_sections_pieces_inf (i j : D.index)
    (hinf : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf

end AffCoverData

/-! ## The optional chart typing, for the Θ-layer only -/

/-- The pinned chart of a given side, spelled here so this file needs no import from the
Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/
noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀

/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the

`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`, restated here because that one is file-private). -/
private lemma res_res' {X : Scheme.{u}} {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U)
    (s : Γ(X, U)) :
    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]

/-! ## The widened adaptation -/

/-- **The adaptation of a local-equation system to a widened cover.** Identical in content to
`DivisorAdaptation` except that the cover datum is an `AffCoverData`: equations on the pieces,
plus the point-free pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`.

`eqn_rel` quantifies over ALL `y` — on an empty overlap the section ring is the zero ring and
the clause is trivial — which is what makes it pull back along arbitrary morphisms. -/
structure AffAdaptation (D : AffCoverData C R) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Type u where
  /-- The equation on the piece `j`. -/
  eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units. -/
  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C R),
    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)

namespace AffAdaptation

variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)

/-- The index of the adaptation is the index of its cover. -/
abbrev index : Type := D.index

/-- **The anchored constructor.** A base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with
`pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)` and a comparison unit; `eqn_rel` is derived by transporting
`d.eqn (pt j)` to `d.eqn y` through `d.ratioUnit`, exactly as in
`DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`. -/
def ofAnchors
    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
    AffAdaptation D d where
  eqn := eqn
  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
    rw [map_mul, res_res'] at E1
    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
    rw [map_mul, res_res', res_res'] at E2
    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
    rw [Units.val_mul]
    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# DECIDING THE FORK: what non-injectivity of the unrestricted Abel chart actually costs
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` makes the fork precise and machine-checked:
    12	`IsChartLocusFibre` implies the Abel chart is a monomorphism, which three headers
    13	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
    14	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`) assert it is not.  Exactly one side is right, and
    15	the guard leaves the deciding statement — non-injectivity — as prose.
    16	
    17	**This file reduces that statement to divisor data.**  The reduction is what was missing: the
    18	Abel chart's app does not take divisors, it takes `D.left`-points, so "two divisors in one
    19	linear system" is not by itself a witness.  Reading `abelChartApp_eq`
    20	(`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`), a point `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is sent to the **pair**
    21	
    22	  `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl))⟩`
    23	
    24	so a non-injectivity witness owes *two* agreements, not one: the Σ-components `x ≫ D.hom` must
    25	agree before the classes are in the same type at all.  That is the trap the c9b row names.
    26	
    27	## What is proved here
    28	
    29	The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs, and its converse:
    30	
    31	* `not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points` — from two `D.left`-points over one test with
    32	  **equal structure morphism** and **equal chart value** but distinct as points, the Abel chart
    33	  fails to be injective; `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points` composes that with the guard to
    34	  refute `IsChartLocusFibre`.
    35	* `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar` — the same reduction **reparameterised onto divisor
    36	  families**: two distinct elements of `divFamZar C π n T` with equal chart value.  Here the
    37	  Σ-component hypothesis is not passed in: both points are `(rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ).left`, whose
    38	  structure morphism is the test's own by `Over.w`, so `hstruct` holds by construction.
    39	  **This is a change of parameterisation, not a strengthening** — the two forms are
    40	  inter-derivable (from the family form, take `T := Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and use
    41	  `rep.homEquiv.injective` for distinctness), so `hstruct` is absorbed by the choice of test
    42	  rather than eliminated.  Its value is that the family form is the shape a divisor argument
    43	  produces, with no scheme-theoretic side condition to discharge first.
    44	* `abelChartApp_inj_iff` — the unfolded shape of injectivity at a test, by `Iff.rfl`.  A
    45	  documentation lemma only: it has no call site below, and `abelChartApp_eq`
    46	  (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`) already exposes both components.
    47	
    48	## What is NOT proved here, stated so this file is not over-read
    49	
    50	**Nothing here exhibits a curve on which the hypothesis holds, and no theorem below closes the
    51	fork.**  Every statement here is an implication whose antecedent is open.  What remains is
    52	exactly:
    53	
    54	  for some curve, some test `T`, and some `n`: two *distinct* elements of `divFamZar C π n T`
    55	  whose `chartValue` agree.
    56	
    57	Three things to know before pricing that, and the third is the one that moves.
    58	
    59	1. Over a field test it is the classical `h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≥ 2 ⇒ |D|` has two points.
    60	   `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
    61	   is the exact boundary: uniqueness holds **at** `h⁰ = 1`, so the hypothesis to arrange is
    62	   `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  It is the statement to contradict, not to apply.
    63	2. The passage from two *divisors* to two distinct *elements of `divFamZar`* is not free: the
    64	   families are a quotient of local-equation data (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`), so distinct
    65	   divisors need not give distinct families until that equivalence is read.  Nothing here
    66	   assumes otherwise.
    67	3. **`n` is not free.**  At `n = g` the chart's own degree calibration makes the *fibrewise*
    68	   linear system a single point for free: over a field `K`, an effective `K`-divisor of degree
    69	   `g` with `Subsingleton H¹` has `h⁰ = 1` exactly (`degAt_chartTwist`'s `+g` discussion in
    70	   `Pic0ChartLocus.lean:178-201`, and the rank anchor
    71	   `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`, `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`, giving
    72	   `h⁰ = g + (1 − g) = 1`).  So the *fibrewise* form of the headers' reason — a
    73	   positive-dimensional `|D|` — is unavailable at `n = g` wherever `H¹` vanishes.
    74	
    75	**AND HERE IS THE LIMIT OF THAT OBSERVATION, which item 3 must not be read past.**  Every anchor
    76	in item 3 is fibrewise over one field: `CurveDivisor` over `K`, `h⁰` a `finrank` over `K`,
    77	`degAt` evaluated at `overSpec k K`-points.  The obligation is **general-test**: injectivity of
    78	`.app (op Y)` at arbitrary `Y`, and correspondingly distinctness in `divFamZar C π n T` at
    79	arbitrary `T`.  A fibrewise anchor does not settle a general-test statement, and the brick that
    80	would bridge them is *relative* GAP-2 — exactly `ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor`
    81	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`), which `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:160-161` names as
    82	"the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2" and which **nothing in the tree produces**: no declaration
    83	concludes `s₁ = s₂` for two `divFamZar` sections from an equality of their classes.
    84	
    85	So item 3 **relocates** the fork; it does not shrink it.  What it changes is what a witness
    86	should aim at: a bare "two divisors in one linear system" is the wrong target, because at `n = g`
    87	with `h¹ = 0` there are none fibrewise — so a witness wants a point of the divisor scheme where
    88	`H¹` fails to vanish, or a genuinely relative failure of uniqueness that no fibre sees.  Which
    89	of those two it is, is undecided here.  (The degree-`g`/`h⁰ = 1` link is `ajcr-p4`'s measurement,
    90	I-0888; the fibrewise/general-test caveat is a fresh-context review's, I-0923/I-0924.)
    91	-/

    98	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    99	
   100	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   101	
   102	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   103	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
   104	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   105	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	noncomputable section
   108	
   109	variable {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   110	variable (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   111	variable (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   112	  = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   113	
   114	/-! ## The exact shape of injectivity at a test -/
   115	
   116	/-- **Injectivity of the Abel chart at a test, unfolded.**
   117	
   118	`abelChartApp_eq` is `rfl`, so injectivity of the app at `op Y` is *literally* injectivity of
   119	the pair-valued map below.  Recorded as an `Iff` on the nose so that a lane attacking either
   120	branch of the fork works with the two components explicitly and cannot silently drop the
   121	Σ-component. -/
   122	theorem abelChartApp_inj_iff (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
   123	    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y))
   124	      ↔ Function.Injective (fun x : Y ⟶ D.left =>
   125	          (⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
   126	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
   127	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :
   128	            (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y))) :=
   129	  Iff.rfl
   130	
   131	/-! ## The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs -/
   132	
   133	/-- **Two `D.left`-points over one test with the same chart value refute the certificate.**
   134	
   135	The hypotheses are exactly the two agreements `abelChartApp_eq` demands — equal structure
   136	morphism (`hstruct`) and equal chart value after that identification (`hval`) — together with
   137	distinctness of the points themselves.
   138	
   139	Note `hval` is stated at the *transported* family: once `hstruct` identifies the Σ-components,
   140	both chart values live over `Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and the equation typechecks. -/
   141	theorem not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points {Y : Scheme.{u}} (x₁ x₂ : Y ⟶ D.left)
   142	    (hne : x₁ ≠ x₂) (hstruct : x₁ ≫ D.hom = x₂ ≫ D.hom)
   143	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   144	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ rfl))
   145	      = chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   146	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm))) :
   147	    ¬ Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y)) := by
   148	  intro hinj
   149	  refine hne (hinj ?_)
   150	  -- both values are Σ-elements over the *same* structure morphism after `hstruct`
   151	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) hstruct ?_
   152	  -- the transport of `x₂`'s family along `mkCongr hstruct` is `x₂` read over `x₁`'s base
   153	  have hmap : (divFunctor C π n).map (Over.mkCongr hstruct).op
   154	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ rfl))
   155	      = rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm) := by
   156	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]

measurement of that obligation (`I-0667`) is **33 textual `partition₀`/`partition₁` hits across 11

import closure) a file-level count cannot decide the question: a module can sit in an import cone

This module answers it at the level that matters, in two forms.

endpoints and of two chart-typed **controls**, reporting which mention the `FinCoverData` carrier.

| declaration | closure | mentions `FinCoverData`? |

| `exists_affAdaptation_isCertified_of_straddling` | 4270 | **no** |

A dependency walk is evidence about *proof terms*, which no `#print axioms` and no build checks for

It does **not** say the 49-file consumer migration of `I-0667` is unnecessary. The two measurements

noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀

/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops
the old fixed-pair typing from being smuggled back in through a field. -/
structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
  side : D.index → Bool
  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)

/-! ## Migration: old cover data instantiates the widened datum -/

namespace FinCoverData

variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)

/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
covers together with `relCover_sup`.

The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
content of R2. -/
noncomputable def toAffCoverData : AffCoverData C R where
  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
  cover := by
    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩

@[simp]
lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl

/-- The canonical chart typing of a migrated datum: chart-0 pieces are basic opens of `V₀`,
chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/
noncomputable def toChartTyping : ChartTyping C R π D.toAffCoverData where
  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
  piece_le := fun j => by
    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]

## ADDENDUM 12 (2026-07-29, run 0070 session 0019) — THE FIXED PAIR CAME BACK AS AN INDEX, and an index is not a hypothesis (BINDING)

`I-0492` clause 3 forbids smuggling the old typing back in "by typing pieces INTO the charts".
It was smuggled back in anyway, in a form clause 3's wording does not obviously cover and which
no `sorry` census, job count or axiom probe can see: **as the index type of a layer.**

### 12.1 What happened

`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean` (run 0071, lane `ajcr-divrep`) builds the Θ-layer over a
widened cover, indexed by `τ : ChartTyping C R π D` — a *separate* datum, exactly as clause 3
permits, whose field `piece_le` says each piece lies in one of the two pinned charts. A
fresh-context review (`I-0779`) then proved, in that same file, that a cover with a **straddling**
piece admits **no** `ChartTyping` (`isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling`). So every declaration in
the layer is vacuous on precisely the divisors `I-0492`'s widening exists to serve.

**The methodological error, and it is worth stating separately from the fix.** Clause 3 says no
certificate clause may *require* a chart typing. That is a statement about what is **permitted**.
Whether anything **inhabits** the index is a different question, and only the second decides
whether a layer stated over it computes. A separate datum satisfies clause 3 and can still be
empty — at which point the layer is formally fine, kernel-green, axiom-clean, and useless.
Generalisable: **check inhabitation of an index before pricing anything stated over it.**

### 12.2 The distinction both the old index and its docstring conflated

This is the part worth carrying to other lanes, because the two things are spelled almost alike:

* `relThetaSections` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:59`) models `𝒪(Θᵃ)` as **pairs of sections
  on `V₀`, `V₁` matching through the theta cocycle**. That is a two-chart model of the LINE
  BUNDLE and constrains no divisor: it is how this project spells the sheaf, for *every* family,
  straddling or not.
* `ChartTyping` constrains **the divisor's own pieces** to sit inside those same charts.

Only the second is the refuted fixed-pair confinement (ADDENDUM 3 §2, leaf `…joint-cover`,
rejected). The Θ-layer needs the first and was given the second. Because both mention `V₀`/`V₁`,
a closure probe for `relPinnedChart` cannot tell them apart — §11.4(a)'s probe reported
`relPinnedChart` present via the seed and called it "a limit on the claim, not a breach", which
was right about the seed and would have been the *wrong* verdict here.

### 12.3 The fix, landed

`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean` (`2b8cef366`, `4d975132a`, `6dc39641f`; rooted,
sorry-free, `lake build … EXIT=0`, 8701 jobs, no warning naming the file):

```
structure ThetaTrivData (D : AffCoverData C R) (a : ℕ)
  read j    : relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
  unit i j  : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ
  matching  : res (read i x) = unit i j * res (read j x)
  germ_read : germ (read j x) = u * germ (relThetaResSide a b _ x)   -- u a STALK unit
```

No `piece_le`, and nothing in it says where a piece lies. Then:

* `ChartTyping.thetaTrivData` — the old index maps in, so nothing landed is lost and the
  chart-typed layer is the special case it always was;
* `AffCoverData.thetaTrivDataZero` — **every** widened cover carries one at `a = 0`, straddling
  ones included. At `a = 0` the cocycle is trivial, so a theta section **glues** to a genuine
  global section over `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` — a statement about the CURVE, used before any piece is
  named, which is exactly why it is not a confinement;
* `nonempty_thetaTrivData_and_isEmpty_chartTyping` — the **separation**, in one statement: on a
  straddling cover the new index is inhabited and `ChartTyping` is empty;
* `ker_trivGluedEval` / `ker_trivWindowCarve` / `trivWindowQuotEquiv` — the layer through left
  exactness and the window carve, on the new index.

**Why the kernel bridge survives the weakening, which is the mathematical content.** Chart-typed,
the germ of the reading *is* the germ of the assigned chart component, because the reading is a
restriction. Chart-free they agree only up to a **unit of the stalk** — and a stalk ideal absorbs
units (`Ideal.unit_mul_mem_iff_mem`), so the argument is unchanged. That unit is the entire slack
that buys chart-freedom. `ker_trivWindowCarve`'s right-hand side is `divisorWindow d hH1`, the
same submodule the chart-typed and `ChartTyping`-indexed versions land on, so a consumer switching
index changes no statement downstream.

### 12.4 What is NOT claimed, so the next session does not over-read this

* **Inhabitation at `a > 0` is open and is not free.** It needs `𝒪(Θᵃ)` trivial over each piece,
  i.e. a condition on the BUNDLE over an arbitrary affine open (a class in that piece's `Pic`).
  The file makes that a hypothesis about the *sheaf*, dischargeable per cover, in place of an
  index no straddling cover inhabits at all. That is a strict improvement and not a closure.
  `a = 0` is nonetheless not a vacuous corner: it is the exponent at which
  `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` reads the divisor's own class (`thetaIdealUnit_zero`,
  `Picard/DivisorDatumInverse.lean:207`).
* **Surjectivity of the widened evaluation is untouched** — the right-exactness heart, open before
  this addendum and open after it, on both indices. Nothing here shrinks it.
* The lane's geometric residue of §11.6 is unchanged.

restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that

  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
